NB using this approach "$abc=-2b^3+4b^2+16b$ which is even hence proven" is not sufficient – they would need to say e.g. which is even + even + even or factor out the 2.

accepted.label: a
accepted.text: Note that just $(2-\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{5}{4})^5=\frac{243}{32}$ or $(2-\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{5}{4})^5=(2-\frac{1}{2})^5=\frac{243}{32}$ scores no marks as the $2-\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{5}{4}$ or $2-\frac{1}{2}$ must be evaluated for the M mark.

accepted.label: b
accepted.text: If awarding this mark for the $x^2$ term you can condone missing brackets e.g. $\pm{}^5C_2\times2^3\times\pm\frac{2}{5}x^2$

accepted.label: a
accepted.text: Allow this mark if they add the areas of individual trapezia e.g. $\frac{\text{their }h}{2}\{3+2.6833\}+\frac{\text{their }h}{2}\{2.6833+2.4\}+\frac{\text{their }h}{2}\{2.4+2.1466\}+\frac{\text{their }h}{2}\{2.1466+1.92\}$ Condone copying slips but must be a complete method using all the trapezia.

accepted.label: b
accepted.text: Must be as shown and not just e.g. $x^{-\frac{1}{2}}(2x^3-10x^2+13x-5)=0$ but allow e.g. $x^{-\frac{1}{2}}(2x^3-10x^2+13x-5)=0$ followed by a minimal conclusion e.g. hence proven.

accepted.label: c
accepted.text: Some candidates are doing the work for part (c) in part (b) so allow the marks for (c) to score in (b) i.e. mark parts (b) and (c) together.

accepted.label: d
accepted.text: Alt(d): You can condone slips when collecting terms or for a slip with brackets e.g. attempting: $\int_0^2 x^3-5x^2+3x+14-\frac{1}{3}x+\frac{22}{3}\,dx$

accepted.label: ii
accepted.text: Note that this may follow incorrect work e.g. $3^x\times2^{x+4}=6\Rightarrow\log_2 3^x\times\log_2 2^{x+4}=\log_2 6\Rightarrow x\log_2 3\times(x+4)\log_2 2^{x+4}=\log_2 6$

accepted.label: ii
accepted.text: dM1 examples: $x\log_2 3+(x+4)\log_2 2=\log_2 6\Rightarrow x(\log_2 3+\log_2 2)=\log_2 6-4\Rightarrow x=...$ or $(x-1)\log_2 3+(x+3)\log_2 2=0\Rightarrow ax+x=a-3\Rightarrow x=...$

accepted.label: ii
accepted.text: Alternative using change of base: $3^x\times2^{x+4}=6\Rightarrow2^{x+3}=3^{1-x}\Rightarrow\log2^{x+3}=\log3^{1-x}\Rightarrow(x+3)\log2=(1-x)\log3\Rightarrow(x+3)\frac{\log_2 2}{\log_2 10}=(1-x)\frac{\log_2 3}{\log_2 10}\Rightarrow x+3=a(1-x)\Rightarrow x(a+1)=a-3\Rightarrow x=...$ Score as: M1: Divides by 2 and $3^x$ and takes logs of both sides B1: E.g. $\log2^{x+3}=(x+3)\log2$ or $\log3^{1-x}=(1-x)\log3$ dM1: Changes to base 2 correctly and makes x the subject as main scheme A1: $\frac{a-3}{a+1}$ or e.g. $\frac{3-a}{-a-1}$

accepted.label: ii
accepted.text: Alternative using logs base 6: $3^x\times2^{x+4}=6\Rightarrow3^x\times2^x=\frac{3}{8}\Rightarrow6^x=\frac{3}{8}\Rightarrow\log_6 6^x=\log_6\frac{3}{8}\Rightarrow x\log_6 6=\log_6\frac{3}{8}$, $x=\log_6\frac{3}{8}=\frac{\log_2\frac{3}{8}}{\log_2 6}=\frac{\log_2 3-\log_2 8}{\log_2 3+\log_2 2}=\frac{a-3}{a+1}$ M1: Divides by $2^4$, writes $3^x\times2^x$ as $6^x$ and takes logs base 6 of both sides which may be implied by e.g. $6^x=\frac{3}{8}\Rightarrow x=\log_6\frac{3}{8}$ B1: For $\log_6 6^x=x\log_6 6$ (may be implied) dM1: Changes to log base 2 correctly (and makes x the subject) A1: Correct expression
